purpose: Live Power Stack thematic radar. Theme rank changes research priority, action thresholds and proof requirements; it does not mechanically change company fundamental scores.

environment.label: Inflationary physical-capex expansion confronting a global duration shortage
environment.summary: Energy/product inflation, sovereign and AI debt supply, and Japan monetary normalisation are colliding in the global duration market while physical AI/grid demand remains strong.

promoteWhen: Fresh material evidence changes transmission or investability
At least two independent research streams converge
parkWhen: Transmission weakens or is absorbed by a broader theme
Narrative rises without commercial or balance-sheet evidence

methodology.recencyRule: Weight the last four days most heavily inside a 14-day window
methodology.ratesRule: Separate own-funding, customer-funding, valuation-duration and capex sensitivity
methodology.aiFundingRule: Funded backlog and contracted cash flow outrank announced capacity
methodology.macroMicroRule: MacroMicro is a supporting cross-market verification layer; fresher official releases control where the aggregator lags.

regimeModifiers.name: Global Duration Absorption Shortage
regimeModifiers.summary: The marginal buyer must absorb Treasury supply, AI/corporate/project issuance and less-suppressed Japanese duration while energy inflation keeps real and nominal yields high.

themes.name: Global Duration Absorption Stress
themes.summary: The macro problem is no longer simply Fed policy. Treasury supply, AI-related debt, project finance and Japan normalisation are competing for the same long-duration capital.
themes.whyNow: MacroMicro shows US10Y 4.79%, real10Y 2.42% and Japan10Y 2.89%. IG OAS remains only 0.81% while CCC OAS is 10.55%, pointing to high clearing yields and weak-end stress rather than a broad credit crisis.
themes.marketTransmission: Higher hurdle rates, tighter project underwriting, lower equity duration tolerance and greater dispersion between cash-generative scarcity and financing-dependent growth.
themes.nextTest: Sep 10 PPI, Sep 11 CPI, Sep 15-16 FOMC, Sep 17-18 BOJ and the post-event long-end response.
themes.invalidation: Sustained compression in long-end yields and credit spreads with improving duration demand.

mainNews.title: MacroMicro confirms restrictive US and Japan duration backdrop
mainNews.implication: The US10Y/JGB combination validates a global rather than Fed-only duration problem.

themes.name: Middle East Refined Products + Shipping Stress
themes.summary: Iran/Houthi escalation has broadened beyond crude and Hormuz into vessels, Saudi infrastructure, refinery/product constraints and bypass-route vulnerability.
themes.whyNow: Brent settled $97.92 after trading above $99, Hormuz commodity traffic remains depressed and US refiners are near capacity while diesel/product tightness transmits directly into transport and inflation.
themes.marketTransmission: Refining margins, tanker rates, insurance, diesel/jet inflation, transport costs, farmer inputs and bond yields.
themes.nextTest: EIA product data and any change in Saudi/Hormuz physical flows.
themes.invalidation: Normalised flows plus sustained collapse in product cracks, insurance and freight.

mainNews.title: Refining bottlenecks become the next energy constraint
mainNews.implication: Refiners can retain strong economics even if Brent itself stabilises.

themes.name: Power / Grid / Cooling + Peak-Load Resilience
themes.summary: Observed peak-load and cooling stress in California and Malaysia turns the power bottleneck from forecast demand into operating evidence.
themes.whyNow: CAISO issued a Flex Alert/EEA1 during heat and Malaysia data centres reached a record 9.3% share of electricity demand in August heat.
themes.marketTransmission: Benefits existing dispatchable generation, regulated grid, substations, switchgear, transmission and cooling while raising project input requirements.
themes.nextTest: Repeated peak-stress events and new firm-load/network awards.
themes.invalidation: Cancelled interconnections, weak utilisation or normalised capacity margins despite new load.

themes.name: AI Financial Structure + Cash Conversion
themes.summary: AI demand remains strong, but financing structure is now a macro variable. Debt supply, guarantees, SPVs, warrants and project-finance terms determine which growth creates equity value.
themes.whyNow: The Goldman/JPMorgan/Reuters evidence shows AI debt issuance is macro-sized while lenders increasingly require permits, leases, guarantees and sponsor support.
themes.marketTransmission: Credit spreads can lead equity stress by raising project hurdle rates before end demand visibly breaks.
themes.nextTest: Any new large AI financing plus spread behaviour into Q4's expected issuance pause.
themes.invalidation: Falling spreads and financing costs with strong cash conversion and no backlog deterioration.

themes.name: AI Physical Buildout + Funded Demand
themes.summary: Physical AI demand remains real, but funded orders and energised capacity now matter more than proposed megawatts.
themes.whyNow: Peak-load evidence and supplier backlogs remain strong even as the financing market becomes more selective.
themes.marketTransmission: Supports generation, transmission, electrical equipment, thermal management and construction companies with actual awards and pricing power.
themes.nextTest: Supplier order/backlog updates and cancellation rates.
themes.invalidation: Broad funded-backlog erosion rather than isolated project delays.

themes.name: Japan Normalisation + Global Liquidity
themes.summary: Japan is shifting from a passive source of cheap global duration toward a higher-yield domestic alternative and potential carry-unwind catalyst.
themes.whyNow: MacroMicro shows Japan10Y 2.89% and a 1.06pp 10Y-2Y curve spread while BOJ runoff, intervention and yen strength make overseas duration less automatically attractive.
themes.marketTransmission: JPY carry unwind, foreign-bond demand, US Treasury demand, equity liquidity and global term premium.
themes.nextTest: BOJ Sep 17-18 and Japanese weekly securities-flow data.
themes.invalidation: Orderly BOJ normalisation with stable overseas bond demand and no carry deleveraging.

themes.name: Energy Security Rerouting + Bypass Vulnerability
themes.summary: Rerouting can cap outright crude upside, but the pipelines, ports and refineries that enable adaptation are becoming strategic targets themselves.
themes.whyNow: The Saudi attacks weaken the simple assumption that bypass capacity permanently neutralises Hormuz risk.
themes.marketTransmission: Supports tankers, LNG, storage and alternative corridors while preserving a demand-destruction cap on crude.
themes.nextTest: Whether bypass infrastructure remains operational and whether Asian demand recovers.
themes.invalidation: Durable de-escalation and restored Gulf logistics.

themes.name: Gold: Reserve Diversification vs Real Yields
themes.summary: Central-bank accumulation and fiscal/duration stress strengthen strategic gold, but high real yields still dominate tactical timing.
themes.whyNow: MacroMicro's PBOC series confirms official reserve growth through July while fresher August data extend the buying streak; US real10Y remains 2.42%.
themes.marketTransmission: Supports physical gold and quality miners when sovereign demand offsets opportunity cost; vulnerable to abrupt real-yield spikes.
themes.invalidation: Persistent real-yield/USD breakout with bullion losing major support.

themes.name: China Weak Credit Transmission + State Balance Sheets
themes.direction: weak private transmission / stronger state support
themes.summary: China can recapitalise institutions and fund state infrastructure without producing a normal household/private credit boom.
themes.whyNow: MacroMicro shows credit impulse 20.84 versus 21.03 prior and a negative July TSF RMB-loan increase, reinforcing the dossier's weak-demand interpretation.
themes.marketTransmission: Favours state-backed power, infrastructure and verified exporters over property, broad consumer reflation and leverage-dependent private demand.
themes.nextTest: August/September China credit and activity data.
themes.invalidation: Sustained rebound in household/private credit, property and retail demand.

themes.name: Copper: Grid Scarcity vs China Divergence
themes.summary: Record copper validates scarcity and grid demand but should not be treated as proof of broad Chinese reflation.
themes.whyNow: Copper hit records while MacroMicro's China credit impulse remains soft, creating a useful divergence between industrial scarcity and domestic credit demand.
themes.marketTransmission: Benefits producers but raises input costs for electrical, grid and construction beneficiaries without pricing power.
themes.nextTest: Inventory draws and China demand confirmation.
themes.invalidation: Inventory rebuild plus weaker grid/industrial orders.

themes.name: Fertilizer / Nitrogen Scarcity vs Farm Affordability
themes.summary: Energy and shipping shocks support nitrogen pricing while higher diesel and fertilizer costs squeeze farmer margins.
themes.invalidation: Normalised feedstock/logistics plus weak farm demand overwhelming pricing.

themes.name: Consumer Credit + Trade-Down Bifurcation
themes.summary: Consumers are still borrowing, but higher energy and financing costs reduce future flexibility rather than signalling an immediate collapse.
themes.whyNow: Revolving credit remains high while energy and long-rate pressure worsen debt-service economics.
themes.marketTransmission: Favours pawn/trade-down/collateral-credit models and penalises rate-sensitive discretionary spending.
themes.invalidation: Broad improvement in real income and delinquency while financing costs fall.

themes.name: Uranium / Nuclear Fuel-Cycle Scarcity
themes.summary: Nuclear security remains structurally attractive, but operating fuel/components outrank financing-heavy pre-revenue reactor equities.

themes.name: Selective Automation Before Humanoids
themes.summary: Commercial automation remains investable where ROI and cash conversion are visible; funding-sensitive humanoid narratives move lower in the current duration regime.
themes.invalidation: Broad deterioration in real customer ROI or order conversion.
